book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Greeting head of state with panic, say

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of state is used

parts.note: its first letter is the head of the word

indicators.note: signals that the word for panic is taken by how it sounds rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: alarm is sudden fear; said in a non-rhotic British accent it sounds like 'a-laam'

explanation.surface: A president's greeting arrives with a hint of panic in it, as if delivered nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone relies on a British accent that drops the R, so alarm is heard as 'alaam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a ceremonial Eastern salutation, often made with a low bow and a hand to the forehead.

clue.text: Wander around in a dream, bleary-eyed

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words, spanning dream and bleary

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of dream into the start of bleary

explanation.surface: Someone half awake drifts about the house in a daze, eyes still bleary.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, strolling about without hurry.

clue.text: Real thin with a cute bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a model: genuinely slim, with an attractive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like part of the body in the picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is genuine, not fake or counterfeit.

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for tin

parts.note: tin is one example of a metal, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A can of food on the shelf turns out to hold new nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the food in the tin, but it is the definition in its sense of crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for crazy or out of one's mind.

clue.text: Chopping cocaine, getting out of it!

parts.note: C is the slang abbreviation for cocaine
getting out of a place is leaving it

explanation.surface: A drug user cutting up lines of cocaine is urged to get out of the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopping cocaine' reads as one picture of cutting the drug, and 'out of it' suggests being high; the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or hack apart, as with an axe or cleaver.

clue.text: Cooking novice once fed on this?

definitions.text: Cooking novice once fed on this?

indicators.note: cooking the books means fiddling them, so the letters that follow are reworked

parts.note: these four words supply the fifteen letters to be cooked

explanation.surface: Someone who could not cook used to live on this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the anagram fodder runs from novice to on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready meals that need only reheating are what someone with no kitchen skills tends to survive on.

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or squandered, so these letters are taken apart and rearranged

parts.note: these two words are the letters to be wasted

explanation.surface: A pensioner regrets the years thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor or official who has retired but keeps an honorary title.

definitions.meaning: read as 'a sign', one of the twelve signs of the zodiac
the sign whose emblem is the virgin, a symbol of chastity

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Assign' into 'A sign' and the clue asks for the star sign represented by a virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: This zodiac sign takes its name from the Latin for virgin, embodying purity.

definitions.meaning: a brown study is a daydream, but here it is the study of Gordon Brown, the UK Prime Minister 2007-10
asks for the place where that office is located

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown study' is a set phrase for a reverie; read literally it is Gordon Brown's study, at 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's London residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Prime Minister's official home is universally known by its street address in Downing Street.

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a need is a lack or absence of something
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether, if pushed, they could manage to stay sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb at the start of a question; it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from alcohol, which is what sobriety means.

clue.text: Beginning to run or maybe play

definitions.text: Beginning to run or maybe play

indicators.note: the beginning of each of the following words supplies one letter

parts.note: its first letter starts the answer
its first letter comes second
its first letter comes third
its first letter ends the answer

explanation.surface: A child starts running about, or perhaps playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the last four words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to run about and play boisterously, as children do.

clue.text: Drink beer's head, always before time

indicators.note: the word for always comes ahead of the word for time
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is the head of the beer
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Drink the froth on your beer straight away, before time is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beer's head' suggests froth on a pint, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a liquid for drinking.

definitions.meaning: read as 'de-creased', having had the creases taken out
the chore that takes creases out of laundry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreased' looks like 'reduced'; split it as de-creased and it describes pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron smooths away wrinkles, a routine household chore.

indicators.note: going back means this word for strikes is read from right to left

parts.note: taps are light strikes or blows

explanation.surface: Someone hits back during a trivial quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief, minor quarrel over something trivial.

indicators.note: something crashing is smashed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters that go crashing

explanation.surface: A tedious person keeps telling the same story again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' wants to be the tedious person; it is the verb meaning drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate something is to pierce or drill holes through it.

indicators.note: to regroup is to reorganise, so the letters are reorganised into a new word

parts.note: these two words give the letters that regroup

explanation.surface: A rallying call to a defeated army to come together, re-form and crush the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or swamp, overwhelming with a great quantity.

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, and the possessive adds the S
a mantle is a cloak or covering layer

explanation.surface: An undercover detective's false identity is about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is Detective Inspector, and the possessive supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take something apart piece by piece.

indicators.note: the word for play comes after the word for penalties

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A football report: some subtle passing after the penalty shootout.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun describes something extremely fine, intricate or thin in texture.

indicators.note: the word for lies goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: fiction is invented untruth

explanation.surface: Untruths told about who was in the right cause bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is conflict or rubbing between people, a source of annoyance.

parts.note: a son is a male child

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is the group's opening

explanation.surface: A boy band starts its concert with a particular track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a numeral; it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number is a song or piece in a performance.

clue.text: Ends of short dress giving flash

indicators.note: only the two end letters of the word short are used

parts.note: its first and last letters are its ends
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: A very short hemline reveals a flash of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a light that gives rapid repeated bursts of brightness.

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the word for nucleus

parts.note: the core of something is its central part

explanation.surface: A bomb-maker plants explosive at the heart of a reactor.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together or adhere, forming a united whole.

definitions.meaning: the plain meaning, boredom or listlessness
Nicolas Sarkozy, French president 2007-12, would use the French word for it

explanation.walkthrough: The word for boredom is borrowed from French, so it is what a Frenchman like Sarkozy might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a French loanword.

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of Parliament through ran into the start of centrist

explanation.surface: A political report: a moderate faction in Parliament launched a lobbying campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' wants to be the verb of political pressure; it is the hall inside a building's door.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is the hall or foyer at the way into a building.

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A dog-handler in the army joins a company of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: The fleet is on high alert for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alert' looks like an adjective; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to warn them of danger, giving notice.

indicators.note: the new party member comes after the publicity

parts.note: a promo is a promotional piece, publicity hype
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A newly elected Tory blusters his way through the media frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like deception or bluntness; it is a steep cliff or headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a broad steep cliff, and a promontory is high land jutting into the sea.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: accepting that something bad cannot be avoided
second meaning: quit a job or post

explanation.walkthrough: A politician who quits in despair fits both senses of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both stoically accepting defeat and having stepped down from a position.

definitions.meaning: a covering, as a lid covers a box
a peeper is slang for an eye, though it suggests a voyeur

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeper' suggests a Peeping Tom needing a disguise; it is slang for the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin closing over the eye shields it like a lid.
